provider: PikPak - free account (cloud download plus downstream)
category: private cloud drive with a cloud-download engine

free_tier.stated: 'Free accounts include 6 GB of storage, and Premium includes 10 TB.' Downstream is metered on every account: 'Free PikPak accounts have a daily Downstream limit of 20 GB, which resets at 0:00 Singapore Time. All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.'
free_tier.notes: Two counters, not one: 20 GB/day for the official apps and 5 GB/day for anything programmatic (WebDAV, CLI, MCP, personal access tokens). The 6 GB store is what the downloaded bytes must pass through, exactly as CloudPipe's 450 GB must pass through a 15 GB Google Drive.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated. No per-object number is published; the limits that bite on a free account are the 6 GB store and three Cloud Download tasks a day.
per_object_cap.notes: A 20 GiB object cannot be held in a 6 GB store at all, so the object cap is the store, not a published file limit.

retention.stated: files stay in the account until deleted, and the free account holds 6 GB, so retention is bounded by capacity rather than by a day count. Non-Premium accounts with no login for 12 consecutive months may be deleted.

egress.terms: Metered in three dimensions per calendar month: cloud download 40 TB, downstream 4 TB, upload 1 TB, then a separate free-account daily downstream cap of 20 GB. 'All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.' Over the limit 'Downstream traffic slows to about 100 KB/s' and 'New Cloud Download tasks are blocked'.
egress.free_allowance: 20 GB/day downstream in the official apps; 5 GB/day for Connected Apps

interface_detail: official apps plus WebDAV, an official CLI, an MCP server and personal access tokens, all grouped by the vendor as 'Connected Apps' and all subject to the 5 GB/day cap
tooling: rclone over WebDAV or the CLI; both land in the Connected Apps bucket and take the quarter allowance
chaining: Adds 150 GB a month to a no-card ladder for one email address, making it the largest per-signup free step that is not CloudPipe. Its counter resets daily, so it repeats in month two.

limits.value: 6 GB of storage on a free account
20 GB/day downstream for the whole free account, resets at 0:00 Singapore Time
5 GB/day downstream for all Connected Apps together (25% of the daily cap)
three Cloud Download tasks a day on a free account

limits_note: The monthly 4 TB downstream quota is not the binding number for a free account; the daily cap is, by a factor of 120.
binding_note: At 5 GB/day a programmatic client gets 150 GB/month and at 20 GB/day an app-only client gets 600 GB/month. Both are below every other group-1 step except Bitport, and both require deleting through a 6 GB store.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is by email. No card and no phone is named on the help-centre pages read; the signup form itself was not opened, so this is the published gate rather than an observed one.

reliability_note: Over the daily cap downstream slows to about 100 KB/s and new cloud-download tasks are blocked while running ones continue; a free account with no login for 12 months may be deleted.
confidence_note: Both counters are vendor sentences read today. No account was created, so neither the 5 GB nor the 20 GB was measured, and the 6 GB store was not filled to see what happens.

evidence.proved: 'Free PikPak accounts have a daily Downstream limit of 20 GB, which resets at 0:00 Singapore Time. All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.' Also the 40 TB / 4 TB / 1 TB monthly tab and the 12-month inactivity deletion.
'Free accounts include 6 GB of storage, and Premium includes 10 TB.'

notes: The number that matters to the ladder is 150 GB/month programmatic, not 600: a user drives the service with a script, and the vendor caps every programmatic path at 25% of the daily allowance.
